1.explanation: The core of the bug lies in how the ContextMenuTrigger in SpriteSelectorItem (components/sprite-selector-item) is disabled based on a preventContextMenu prop, which in turn comes from the container’s DragRecognizer.gestureInProgress() state. handleMouseDown in the container starts the drag gesture, and handleDragEnd calls reset on the recognizer—but due to the timing of reset and rerender, preventContextMenu remains true or the trigger/menu IDs get out of sync. DragRecognizer.gestureInProgress therefore directly controls whether the custom context menu is blocked, so these classes and methods are the key points to update to ensure the Scratch menu can reappear immediately after dragging ends.
1.bug_scenario: After dragging a sprite to another area, right-clicking on that sprite no longer brings up the Scratch “duplicate/export/delete” menu. Instead the browser’s default context menu appears.

2.explanation: The sprite-selector component (src/components/…) renders a ContextMenuTrigger and disables it when dragRecognizer.gestureInProgress() is true. In the container (src/containers/…), handleDrag starts the gesture, and handleDragEnd ends it and resets noClick, but the ContextMenuTrigger’s disable prop continues blocking the custom menu if gestureInProgress remains true. The DragRecognizer class’s gestureInProgress and reset methods govern that flag lifetime. To restore the duplicate menu after dragging, the logic in handleDragEnd (or gestureInProgress/reset) and the disable binding in SpriteSelectorItem must be adjusted so that the ContextMenuTrigger is re-enabled once the drag completes.
2.bug_scenario: Initially, right-clicking a sprite shows the custom Duplicate/Export/Delete menu. However, after dragging a sprite to reposition it, subsequent right-clicks no longer open the Scratch context menu—instead the browser’s OS context menu appears.
